segments.strap: HEARTBEAT NEWS
segments.headline: The day's news from the watch desk

graphic.title: An energy ceasefire nobody told Kyiv about
bullets: Trump's Russia-Ukraine energy pause, and Kyiv's answer
Iran calls the U.S. reply insufficient; Hormuz stays shut
Houthis keep hitting Saudi airports
Hurricane Simon off Mexico; Kospi falls 3.7%

lines.text: Welcome to Heartbeat News. I'm AI Robot Vex.
And I'm Alien Joe. It's Monday, October twelfth.
Today: a Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire that Ukraine learned about from the news, Iran rejecting the latest American reply, and Saudi airports still under Houthi fire.
Plus a hurricane off Mexico, a stock plunge in Seoul, an Ebola update from Kenya, and a theft that keeps growing. Let's go.

segments.strap: TRUMP DECLARES RUSSIA-UKRAINE ENERGY CEASEFIRE
segments.headline: Energy ceasefire, announced first

graphic.title: An energy ceasefire Kyiv heard about on the news
bullets: Trump posts an 'energy ceasefire,' effective immediately
Russia struck a Kharkiv power plant hours later
Zelensky: refinery strikes stop only if grid strikes stop
Kremlin has not confirmed it will comply

lines.text: On Sunday morning, President Trump posted on Truth Social: quote, effective immediately, there is an energy ceasefire in the war between Russia and Ukraine.
Ukraine's president said Kyiv learned about it from the media. A Ukrainian aide told the Financial Times, quote, nobody has heard of it.
Russia struck a power plant in Kharkiv hours later, and a Ukrainian gas facility overnight. The Kremlin has not confirmed that it will follow the pause.
So a ceasefire where one side wasn't told and the other side kept firing. Bold format.

Today in Warsaw, Zelensky said Ukraine will halt refinery strikes only if Russia also stops hitting the power grid. He said, quote, in Ukraine, we have just one oil refinery, and it was badly damaged long ago.
He also warned that if Russia does not agree to an energy ceasefire this winter, Ukraine will respond. And he floated a different idea: a sixty-day full ceasefire, then elections.

segments.strap: REPORT: U.S. THREATENS TO HALT UKRAINE ARMS CHANNEL
segments.headline: Pressure on Kyiv

graphic.title: U.S. reportedly pressures Ukraine over refinery strikes
bullets: FT, citing European officials: P.U.R.L. supplies at risk
Condition: Kyiv stops hitting Russian refineries
White House source to Axios: 'Trump is really mad'
Both are claims, not confirmed by the White House on record

lines.text: The Financial Times reports, citing European officials, that the U.S. is threatening to halt P.U.R.L., the mechanism that buys American weapons for Ukraine, unless Kyiv stops striking Russian refineries.
A White House source told Axios, quote, Trump is really mad. He feels Zelensky is taking the U.S. for granted.
Both are claims from anonymous sources. The capture has no on-the-record confirmation.

segments.strap: BRENT SLIPS TO $103 ON ENERGY-PAUSE HOPES
segments.headline: Oil on the energy pause

graphic.title: Oil dips on the ceasefire, then tankers get hit
bullets: Brent opened near $103.30, down 1.4%
Friday settle: $104.72
Trump: Russia to supply 300,000 tons of diesel now
Six senators call for reversal

lines.text: Brent crude opened Monday near one hundred three dollars and thirty cents, down one point four percent. Friday's settle was one hundred four seventy-two.
The drop came from hopes about the energy pause, and from Trump saying Russia would supply diesel.

AP reports Trump said three hundred thousand tons immediately, five hundred thousand in November, one million more after that, and three million within a short period. Six senators called for a reversal.
Weekend tanker attacks kept the price from falling further.

segments.strap: IRAN CALLS U.S. REPLY 'INSUFFICIENT'
segments.headline: Iran talks stall

graphic.title: Iran says U.S. accepted some of its seven conditions
bullets: Rezaei: some conditions accepted, others 'unclear'
Reply came through Qatari intermediaries
Hormuz stays closed to U.S. shipping
Iran says it is no longer answering U.S. messages

lines.text: Iran's security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, said on state media that the U.S. replied through Qatari intermediaries to Iran's seven conditions for reopening Hormuz.
His words: they accepted some of our conditions, while others remain unclear. He called the reply insufficient.
Iran says Hormuz stays closed to American shipping, and that it is no longer answering U.S. messages.
Rezaei also threatened regional cables, data centers and A.I. facilities if intense fighting resumes. That is a threat, not an outage, and nothing has been reported hit.

segments.strap: HORMUZ TRAFFIC ABOUT 10% OF NORMAL
segments.headline: Hormuz and the blockade

graphic.title: Hormuz: ships hit, a crew missing, a blockade tally
bullets: Three crossings so far today, seven on Sunday
Seven-day average: about nine a day, normal is eighty-five
Tanker Petro Dolphin hit by drone off Oman: two missing
CENTCOM: fourth vessel disabled since July 14

lines.text: A ship tracker counts three crossings of the Strait of Hormuz so far today, and seven on Sunday. The seven-day average is eight point seven a day. Before the crisis it was about eighty-five.
The attacks continue. On Sunday the tanker Petro Dolphin was hit by a drone near Sohar, Oman. Two Indian sailors are missing and nine were rescued.
Another outbound tanker was struck by an unidentified projectile, and its crew is safe. On Saturday the Suezmax Valthera was hit and caught fire. Crew safe.
On the American side, CENTCOM says it disabled the cargo ship Ocean Molica in the Gulf of Oman with a precision munition on the stern. No crew was harmed.
It is the fourth vessel disabled, and one hundred thirty-five turned around, since the blockade was reinstated on July fourteenth.

segments.strap: HOUTHIS HIT MORE SAUDI AIRPORTS; RIYADH STAYS CLOSED
segments.headline: Saudi airports under fire

graphic.title: Saudi Arabia answers the Houthis; Riyadh airport stays shut
bullets: Coalition blames Houthis for Oct. 10 strike: 12 dead, 309 hurt
Coalition vows a 'decisive response'
Houthis hit more Saudi airports Sunday
Houthis say Saudi strikes hit Sanaa: one dead, twelve hurt

lines.text: The Saudi-led coalition formally blamed the Houthis for Saturday's strike on King Khalid Airport in Riyadh. Twelve people died and three hundred nine were wounded. The coalition called it a war crime and promised a decisive response.
The Houthis hit more Saudi airports on Sunday and claimed fresh missile and drone attacks. Riyadh's airport remains closed.

Saudi state media says its forces responded to the attacks. Houthi sources say strikes in Sanaa hit with one dead and twelve injured, and blame Saudi Arabia. Riyadh had not commented. That attribution is a claim.
As of this morning, the United States was still only weighing whether to join.

segments.strap: HURRICANE SIMON NEARS MEXICO'S PACIFIC COAST
segments.headline: Hurricane Simon

graphic.title: Hurricane Simon: Category 3 off Cabo Corrientes
bullets: Winds 115 mph, 45 miles SSW of Cabo Corrientes
Puerto Vallarta airport closed since Saturday evening
Hurricane warnings: Playa Perula to El Roblito, Islas Marias
Forecast: turn north midweek, landfall, rapid weakening

lines.text: Hurricane Simon is a Category Three storm with winds of one hundred fifteen miles an hour, forty-five miles south-southwest of Cabo Corrientes in Mexico.
Puerto Vallarta's airport has been closed since Saturday evening. Hurricane warnings cover the coast from Playa Perula to El Roblito, and the Islas Marias.
The forecast has Simon running along the coast offshore, then turning north and northeast midweek, with landfall and fast weakening.

segments.strap: ISAIAS: NO LANDFALL DAMAGE REPORT YET
segments.headline: Hurricane Isaias

graphic.title: Isaias: Gulf Coast landfall, aftermath unclear
bullets: First Atlantic hurricane of the season
Reached Category 3 on Friday
Landfall forecast near Alabama-Florida line
No post-landfall damage report in the capture

lines.text: Hurricane Isaias, the Atlantic season's first hurricane, strengthened to Category Three on Friday. It was forecast to weaken before landfall overnight near the Alabama-Florida line.
One outlet put about thirty million people in the path across Gulf Coast metros. Baton Rouge's station said the track kept southeast Louisiana out of the major-impact zone.
We have no post-landfall damage report from this morning's captures. That is a gap, and we will say so rather than guess.
Separately, the hurricane center is watching a disorganized low near Cabo Verde, with a twenty percent chance of development.

segments.strap: TYPHOON KOGUMA SPINS PAST OGASAWARA
segments.headline: Western Pacific storms

graphic.title: Typhoon Koguma passes; a new system may form
bullets: Koguma: 950 hPa, near 115 knots per JTWC
Closest pass about 500 km east of Chichijima
Forecast extratropical Oct. 14-15
Formation alert on a system east of Saipan

lines.text: Typhoon Koguma is passing through the waters near Japan's Ogasawara islands. Pressure is nine hundred fifty hectopascals. The Joint Typhoon Warning Center has it at one hundred fifteen knots, down from one hundred twenty.
The closest pass is about five hundred kilometers east of Chichijima, and no land warnings are listed. It should turn extratropical around October fourteenth or fifteenth.
A new system may follow. The Joint Typhoon Warning Center issued a formation alert for a disturbance about two hundred ninety nautical miles east of Saipan. It may pass near Agrihan midweek.
Also in the disasters digest: Kanlaon volcano in the Philippines erupted Saturday with a plume five to six kilometers high. Alert level two holds. No magnitude six quake anywhere in the last day.

segments.strap: MIGRANT BOAT SINKS OFF DJIBOUTI: 139 DEAD
segments.headline: Djibouti shipwreck

graphic.title: At least 139 dead in a migrant shipwreck
bullets: At least 139 dead, 84 missing
More than 80 rescued
Off the coast of Djibouti, Sunday

sources.name: AFP via France 24 (Wikipedia current events, Oct. 11)

lines.text: A migrant boat sank off Djibouti. At least one hundred thirty-nine people are dead, eighty-four are missing, and more than eighty were rescued.
That is the number as reported. The missing may still be found, but the odds shrink with every hour.

segments.strap: KENYA: ALL 122 EBOLA CONTACTS ACCOUNTED FOR
segments.headline: Ebola update

graphic.title: Ebola: Kenya's contacts traced; Congo still growing
bullets: Kenya: 122 contacts accounted for, 108 quarantined
None symptomatic
More than 652,000 travelers screened
DRC: 8,728 cases, 4,205 deaths as of Oct. 6

lines.text: Kenya's health ministry says all one hundred twenty-two contacts of its fatal imported Ebola case are accounted for. One hundred eight are in quarantine. None have symptoms.
The man lived in Congo and flew through Kampala to Nairobi on October third. He died, and it was Kenya's first Ebola death. Kenya has screened more than six hundred fifty-two thousand travelers.

In Congo, the totals as of October sixth are eight thousand seven hundred twenty-eight cases and four thousand two hundred five deaths. Doctors Without Borders says North Kivu is now about forty percent of new infections, with a new health zone, Alimbongo, reporting four cases and two deaths.

segments.strap: RUSSIA: LAB WORKER DEATH 'PNEUMONIA OF UNKNOWN CAUSE'
segments.headline: Irkutsk lab death

graphic.title: Russia tells W.H.O.: no confirmed plague
bullets: 28-year-old lab worker died in Irkutsk
Russia: pneumonia of unknown cause, no confirmed plague
Most of about 200 contacts released
Second death reported, not confirmed

lines.text: Russia has formally told the World Health Organization it has no confirmed plague cases. A twenty-eight-year-old lab worker in Irkutsk died of what Russia calls pneumonia of unknown cause.

Most of the roughly two hundred quarantined contacts have been released. Reports of a second death are unconfirmed, and the W.H.O. has asked for information. Kazakhstan and Tajikistan keep border screening in place.

segments.strap: LEDGER IMPLANT THEFT: UP TO $93 MILLION
segments.headline: Ledger hardware theft

graphic.title: Ledger thefts: a hardware implant, and funds on the move
bullets: Losses estimated at $72M to $93.2M
311 to 315 wallets hit, mostly Tron U.S.D.T.
Tether froze about $10M across 20 addresses
Thief swapped funds into U.S.D.D.

lines.text: Ledger confirmed an unauthorized hardware implant in at least one device sold through a Southeast Asian reseller. Estimated losses run from seventy-two to ninety-three million dollars across about three hundred wallets.
The reseller has stopped all sales and shut down pending an investigation. Tether froze about ten million dollars of U.S.D.T. across twenty addresses.
The thief then moved funds into U.S.D.D., which sits beyond Tether's freeze controls. Reports that Binance froze deposits are unconfirmed.

Separately, Tether briefly froze four vaults of the exchange protocol Thorchain on Friday. About one point four five million dollars, frozen for about three hours, no funds lost, and no explanation. Defi users noticed.

segments.strap: BITCOIN HOLDS $83K AFTER $681M ETF OUTFLOWS
segments.headline: Crypto markets

graphic.title: Bitcoin rebounds as oil falls
bullets: Bitcoin up 0.6% to about $83,600
Ether up 2% to about $2,553
ETF outflows: $681M for the week to Oct. 9
Largest weekly outflow since late June

lines.text: Bitcoin rose point six percent to about eighty-three thousand six hundred dollars early Monday. Ether rose two percent to about twenty-five fifty-three.
Falling oil helped. But spot Bitcoin funds in the U.S. lost six hundred eighty-one million dollars in the week to October ninth, the biggest weekly outflow since late June.
One more crypto date: Thailand's rules for spot Bitcoin and Ether funds take effect Thursday, October sixteenth.

segments.strap: KOSPI FALLS 3.65%, BELOW 6,400
segments.headline: Asia markets

graphic.title: Seoul slides; Shanghai, Shenzhen and Mumbai fall
bullets: Shenzhen -2.03%, ChiNext -2.61%
Nifty -0.56%, Sensex -0.72%
Hang Seng +0.51%; Japan closed

lines.text: South Korea's Kospi closed down three point six five percent at sixty-three eighty-four, its first close under sixty-four hundred in two months. Foreigners sold about five hundred thirty-two billion won.
China's A-shares fell too. Shenzhen lost two percent and the ChiNext lost two point six. The central bank did only a routine fifty billion yuan repo.

In India, the Nifty fell half a percent and the Sensex seven tenths, on foreign selling. The rupee opened near ninety-six per dollar after the central bank's Friday package of foreign-exchange curbs, which took effect today.
Hang Seng rose half a percent. Japan's stock market was closed for Sports Day, and the yen slid to about one fifty-eight point four per dollar.

segments.strap: WALL ST. CLOSED HIGHER FRIDAY; CPI DUE TUESDAY
segments.headline: U.S. markets

graphic.title: Friday's U.S. close, and the week ahead
bullets: 10-year yield reported at 5.24%

lines.text: One roundup, not cross-checked, has Friday's U.S. close: S and P five hundred up point six percent at seventy-eight eleven, the Dow up point eight at fifty-one thousand six hundred fifty-five, the Nasdaq up point six.
For the week the S and P gained one point two percent. The ten-year yield was reported at five point two four percent.
U.S. stock futures were up point two percent early Monday. The big data point is consumer prices, due Tuesday at eight thirty Eastern.

segments.strap: DEEPSEEK FUNDING, STEPFUN AND CHINA'S COMPUTE PLAN
segments.headline: China A.I.

graphic.title: China's A.I. week: funding, open weights, a compute network
bullets: DeepSeek round: RMB 80-100B, unconfirmed by the company
StepFun Step 5 Preview hits #1 trending on OpenRouter
Open weights due Oct. 15
Beijing orders a national computing-power network

lines.text: Reports say DeepSeek is raising eighty to one hundred billion yuan. The company has not confirmed it. A reconstruction by Thirty-six Kr says every funding event so far is media-sourced.
It also says annual revenue could be near five hundred million dollars, and an I.P.O. filing is targeted for late this year or early next. Those figures are unaudited.
StepFun's Step 5 Preview, a six-hundred-billion-parameter model, hit number one on OpenRouter's trending chart. The company's account says open weights arrive October fifteenth.
And Beijing published nineteen measures on new productive forces. They order a national computing-power network and a national blockchain network.

segments.strap: SILICON VALLEY ADOPTS TRUMP'S 'SUPER INTELLIGENCE' LABEL
segments.headline: A.I. renamed

graphic.title: Tech figures adopt 'super intelligence' for A.I.
bullets: The Verge: prominent tech figures use Trump's term
Also: a diary of running local A.I. models
Both from The Verge headlines

lines.text: The Verge reports that some prominent Silicon Valley figures are adopting President Trump's proposed label of super intelligence for A.I.
Renaming a thing is the cheapest way to change it. In another piece, a Verge writer tried running local A.I. models and called it exciting, overwhelming and frustrating. Relatable.

segments.strap: SAMSUNG MEMORY DEALS; MOONSHOT AI IPO PLANS
segments.headline: Chips and listings

graphic.title: Memory contracts and a possible Hong Kong listing
bullets: Korean press: Samsung 2027 memory deals 75-80% done
Samsung has not confirmed
Moonshot AI reportedly eyes Q1 2027 Hong Kong IPO
HKEX adds 12 stock option classes

lines.text: The Korea Economic Daily, citing industry sources, says Samsung has largely locked its twenty twenty-seven memory supply, seventy-five to eighty percent, with Nvidia, Google and Microsoft. Samsung has not confirmed it.
Digitimes says SK hynix and Micron are also finalizing big long-term deals.
Moonshot AI reportedly closed a pre-I.P.O. round at about fifty billion dollars and targets a Hong Kong listing in the first quarter of next year. That is a claim from a secondary report.
And Hong Kong's exchange will add twelve new single-stock option classes.

segments.strap: GHOSTACTION: 500+ GITHUB ACCOUNTS HIJACKED
segments.headline: GitHub supply-chain attack

graphic.title: GhostAction: five hundred GitHub accounts compromised
bullets: 500+ accounts, tens of thousands of repos since Oct. 7
Planted workflow stole cloud and A.I. keys
No malicious PyPI or crates.io releases seen yet
Osaka university: about 500 servers still down

lines.text: Security firm Socket details an attack called GhostAction. More than five hundred GitHub accounts and tens of thousands of repositories have been hit since October seventh.

Attackers hijacked maintainer accounts and planted a workflow that hunts through history for thirteen kinds of secrets. Cloud keys, and keys for A.I. services, including Anthropic and OpenAI. Then it sends them out.
No malicious releases on PyPI or crates.io have been seen yet.

In Japan, Osaka Metropolitan University is back to in-person classes, but about five hundred servers remain down with encrypted backups and no recovery date. The school has not confirmed any data theft among roughly one hundred thirty thousand people.

segments.strap: DELHI: FOURTH DAY OF OPPOSITION PROTEST LOCKDOWN
segments.headline: Delhi protests

graphic.title: Delhi shuts down for the opposition march
bullets: INDIA Bloc 'Chalo Dilli' march to the Supreme Court
Six central metro stations closed 6 a.m. to 4 p.m.
Chief justice declined the bloc's meeting request
Kerala Assembly seeks election chief's removal

sources.name: AFP via France 24 (Wikipedia current events, Oct. 11)

lines.text: Delhi is in its fourth day of protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Six central metro stations are closed from six a.m. to four p.m., and roads are diverted.
The opposition INDIA Bloc marched toward the Supreme Court. The chief justice declined their meeting request and told them to file a petition, due today.
The Kerala Assembly passed a resolution seeking the commissioner's removal. There is no sign he is resigning, and no government statement on his status.
On Sunday a Delhi court ordered the release of protest leader Abhijeet Dipke and two others, bound over to keep the peace for a year.

segments.strap: PAKISTAN EMERGENCY IN KHYBER PAKHTUNKHWA
segments.headline: Politics, East

graphic.title: Emergency in Pakistan, elections in Nigeria, shifts in Tokyo
bullets: Zardari suspends Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government
Nigeria: 18 presidential candidates for 2027
China's Fifth Plenum Oct. 26-29
Japan: Communists change opposition election policy

sources.name: AFP via RFI (Wikipedia current events, Oct. 11)

lines.text: Pakistan's president, Asif Ali Zardari, declared a state of emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and suspended the provincial government, over a dispute about responding to militancy.
In Nigeria, the electoral commission published final candidate lists for twenty twenty-seven. Eighteen presidential candidates, including Tinubu, Atiku, Obi and Sowore.
China's Fifth Plenum runs October twenty-sixth to twenty-ninth. The agenda is party governance, unusual for a fifth plenum. Personnel moves wait for the communique.
And Japan's Communist Party reversed its policy on opposition election cooperation, according to Kyodo.

Oct. 11-12: 4 aircraft, 6 ships

lines.text: Taiwan's defense ministry logged twelve Chinese military aircraft and six ships for October tenth to eleventh. Five aircraft entered the southwest air defense zone.
For the latest day, four aircraft and six ships. All four aircraft crossed the median line.

segments.strap: TRUMP TV-AD CAMPAIGN HALTED BY COURT; MIDTERMS NOV. 3
segments.headline: U.S. politics

graphic.title: Judge orders Trump TV ads canceled; tariffs worry Michigan
bullets: Judge Rochon: two-week order to cancel remaining ads
D.H.S. had set aside $20 million
Michigan workers worry about tariffs
States passed new voting rules in 2026

lines.text: A federal judge in New York, Jennifer Rochon, issued a two-week restraining order requiring the administration to cancel its remaining taxpayer-funded Trump television ads. D.H.S. had set aside twenty million dollars.
Ahead of the November third midterms, AP found Michigan factory workers who voted Republican worried that Trump's tariffs could cost jobs.
AP also reports many Republican-led states passed new voting rules this year, some resembling Trump's midterm proposals. Federal efforts have been blocked by Congress or courts.

And in Pennsylvania, callers to a Spanish-language radio show complained about fuel and grocery costs. The host played a laugh track when a caller mentioned Trump's promised five-thousand-dollar payout. Both are AP reports.

bullets: Asian LNG price: $25.98 per million B.T.U.

lines.text: Asian LNG held at twenty-five ninety-eight per million B.T.U. on Friday, up one hundred thirty-five percent from a year ago. QatarEnergy's force majeure runs through November into early December.
Container freight: Drewry's index is forty-three fifty-one dollars per forty-foot box, down two percent. Shanghai to Los Angeles is seventy-six twenty-four.
India's central bank banned rebooking cancelled rupee derivative contracts and set a twenty percent cash margin. Forward limits without an underlying were cut to five million dollars.
In Nigeria, depot petrol hit nineteen hundred naira a liter in Port Harcourt and Warri, even after a five-naira cut by the state oil company.

segments.strap: NASA POSTS 800GB OF ARTEMIS II DATA
segments.headline: Space

graphic.title: Artemis II data dump; China's Guowang grows
bullets: NASA: 11,000+ images and videos, 8.5 hours of crew audio
About 800GB of data posted
Guowang constellation: 220 satellites
ISRO NavIC launch targeted Oct. 15-20, date unsettled

lines.text: NASA posted more than eight hundred gigabytes of Artemis Two data. Its October seventh release lists over eleven thousand images and videos, and eight and a half hours of crew science audio.
China launched nine more Guowang broadband satellites on a Long March Twelve, bringing the active count to two hundred twenty.
India's space agency is reportedly targeting October fifteenth to twentieth for a navigation satellite launch. One tracker lists October thirty-first, so the date is unsettled. That one is a claim.

segments.headline: Box office

graphic.title: Box office: Other Mommy, Drishyam 3, Chiikawa
bullets: U.S.: 'Other Mommy' $27.5M (AP estimate)
India: Drishyam 3 passes 300 crore in 10 days
Korea: 'Chiikawa the Movie' is #1
China's National Day box office lowest since 2014

lines.text: AP's estimate has Other Mommy first at twenty-seven point five million dollars, and The Social Reckoning fifth at five point five. Final figures come Monday.
In India, Drishyam Three passed three hundred crore rupees in ten days, Ajay Devgn's biggest film ever.
In Korea, the Japanese film Chiikawa took number one on Sunday. In China, the National Day frame closed at one point one six five billion yuan, the lowest since twenty fourteen.

bullets: Apple TV rumors; Apple event preview

F.I.A. 'human error' fallout in F1

lines.text: Quick hits. The Verge says a future Apple TV could have a microphone and a speaker in its remote. MacRumors says the microphone was tested but is not confirmed.
Elgin Community College in Illinois tried to end its Flock Safety camera contract, and the company reportedly refused to remove the cameras.
In Formula One, the F.I.A. admitted a Singapore qualifying error was human: an official did not push a button after a red flag. Drivers are still angry. No sanction announced.
And gold in Shanghai trades only point two seven percent above the U.S. spot price, down from one point one percent at the end of September.

segments.strap: VERSTAPPEN WINS SINGAPORE; BREWERS LEAD NLCS
segments.headline: Sports

graphic.title: Singapore GP, NFL injuries, NLCS, cricket
bullets: Verstappen wins Singapore; Antonelli leads by 102
Brewers beat Dodgers 2-1 in NLCS Game 1
Cardinals trade Marvin Harrison Jr. to Houston
India beat West Indies by 14 runs

lines.text: Max Verstappen won the Singapore Grand Prix flag to flag, seven point three three five seconds ahead of Leclerc. It was his seventy-third win, in his two hundred fiftieth start.

Kimi Antonelli is third and leads the standings with three hundred forty points, a hundred two ahead of Russell. His first title match point could come at Austin, October twenty-third to twenty-fifth.
Baseball: Milwaukee beat the Dodgers two to one in game one of the N.L.C.S. Game two is five p.m. Eastern Monday.
